Build SQL predicates for one species' habitat classification

Source: R/frs_habitat_predicates.R
frs_habitat_predicates.Rd

Pure-R helper: takes one species' rules + ranges from frs_params() and returns a named list of SQL boolean expressions ("predicates") — the raw yes/no questions that frs_habitat_classify() embeds in CASE WHEN <pred> THEN TRUE ... to produce the per-species habitat columns.

Usage

frs_habitat_predicates(sp_params, model = "cw", near_river_table = NULL)

Arguments

sp_params

A single-species list with species_code, spawn_gradient_min, spawn_gradient_max, and params_sp: that species' element of frs_params() (its ranges, optional rules, optional spawn_edge_types / rear_edge_types). This is the shape frs_habitat_classify() builds per species.

model

Character. Habitat size model: "cw" (channel width, default) or "mad" (mean annual discharge, mad_m3s).

near_river_table

Character or NULL. Schema-qualified table of distances to the nearest river downstream, as written by frs_near_river(). Required when a spawn or rear rule has a near_river pair, its own or inherited; frs_habitat_classify() builds it and passes it. A rule matches only rows walked at exactly its own measure, threshold and distance_max.

Value

A named list with four character scalars: spawn, rear, lake_rear, wetland_rear. Each is an SQL boolean expression suitable for embedding in CASE WHEN ... THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END. Predicates reference the segmented streams alias s..

Details

Returns four predicates per call: spawn, rear, lake_rear, wetland_rear. Each is a fragment that references columns aliased as s. (the segmented streams table). Caller is responsible for embedding them in a complete query.

Two paths are supported, selected per habitat type by what's present in sp_params:

  1. Rules path — when sp_params$params_sp$rules$<spawn|rear> is non-NULL, the rules YAML is compiled to SQL via .frs_rules_to_sql(). CSV thresholds (gradient + the model's size dimension) are passed as the inheritance fallback for rules that omit explicit thresholds.

  2. CSV-ranges path — pre-rules behaviour. Builds the SQL directly from sp_params$params_sp$ranges + sp_params$params_sp$<spawn|rear>_edge_types.

model picks the size dimension, mirroring bcfishpass parameters_habitat_method.csv. "cw" (default) uses the CSV channel-width ranges (ranges$<spawn|rear>$channel_width). "mad" uses the CSV mean annual discharge ranges (ranges$<spawn|rear>$mad_m3s) against s.mad_m3s instead, on both paths. Under "mad", matching bcfishpass: a species with no MAD thresholds (e.g. BT) gets no stream spawning / rearing from inheriting rules; segments with NULL mad_m3s fail; and rule-level channel_width: (the cw-model river-polygon bypass) is ignored. An explicit mad: [min, max] rule applies under either model. frs_habitat_classify() resolves the model per watershed group.

A river nearby (near_river). A segment can pass a rule's size test (channel width under cw, mad_m3s under mad, inherited or explicit) or lie within a distance downstream of a river. "A river" is a segment at least some size by one of three measures: discharge (mad_m3s), modelled channel width or stream order. A rule gets the condition in one of two ways:

  • Inherited from the thresholds CSV, per stage, beside its gradient, width and MAD ranges: <stage>_river_measure (discharge, channel_width, stream_order, or model, which reads width under cw and discharge under mad; absent is model), the threshold of each measure (<stage>_river_discharge_min, <stage>_river_channel_width_min, <stage>_river_stream_order_min) and <stage>_river_distance_max (m). frs_params() stores the pair as params[[sp]]$near_river. Every rule that inherits thresholds and has a size test takes it. A rule with no size test (under cw, one whose stage has no width range) does not, because the pair would then be its only size test and tighten it. A waterbody_type: R rule inherits like a stream rule: with the bundled channel_width: [0, 9999] that admits a river line with no width that lies near a bigger river, so a consumer that means "the river polygon is the river" sets near_river: false on it.

  • On the rule, overriding what it would inherit:

    near_river:
  discharge_min: 3     # or channel_width_min (m) or stream_order_min
  distance_max: 1000   # m, along the network, downstream

    or near_river: false to opt out of an inherited pair (a no-op on a thresholds: false rule, which inherits nothing).

The size test becomes (<size> OR EXISTS ...); everything else in the rule (edge types, gradient, waterbody tests) still applies. The distance is measured by frs_near_river(), which frs_habitat_classify() runs and passes as near_river_table:

  • from the segment's downstream end, so a long segment whose lower end is within reach passes whole;

  • to the river's bank: a tributary's connector line across the river's polygon is left out, and never counts as the river;

  • only for segments smaller than the threshold by the same measure: a river that large passes or fails on its own size test;

  • within one watershed group's table, and never from a segment with no local watershed code (most side channels); see frs_near_river().

Two consequences to know. A thresholds: false rule with its own mapping and no channel_width or mad has near_river as its only size test, and inherits no gradient, so it tests slope only if it carries gradient:. Under mad, a species with no MAD range, which otherwise gets no stream habitat from inheriting rules, qualifies through near_river where a river is near. near_river (a mapping or false) is not allowed on waterbody_type: L or W rules. Species with no rules compile from ranges directly and get no pair.

Lake / wetland rearing predicates (lake_rear, wetland_rear) are gated on the presence of a waterbody_type: L / waterbody_type: W rule in rear:. Without the rule, the predicate is "FALSE" — the species is not lake or wetland-rearing. With the rule, the predicate is polygon membership, filtered by the rule's optional lake_ha_min / wetland_ha_min. It carries no channel-width or discharge test under either model: the line through a polygon measures its inflow, not the polygon. Connection to spawning is applied after classification, for rules that carry requires_connected: spawning (see frs_habitat()).

Examples

params <- frs_params(csv = system.file("extdata",
  "parameters_habitat_thresholds.csv", package = "fresh"))
sp_params <- list(species_code = "CO",
  spawn_gradient_min = 0,
  spawn_gradient_max = params$CO$spawn_gradient_max,
  params_sp = params$CO)

preds <- frs_habitat_predicates(sp_params)
preds$spawn
#> [1] "((s.edge_type IN (1000, 1100, 2000, 2300) AND s.waterbody_key IS NULL AND s.gradient BETWEEN 0 AND 0.0549 AND s.channel_width BETWEEN 2 AND 9999) OR (s.waterbody_key IN (SELECT waterbody_key FROM whse_basemapping.fwa_rivers_poly) AND s.gradient BETWEEN 0 AND 0.0549 AND s.channel_width BETWEEN 0 AND 9999))"
preds$lake_rear
#> [1] "s.waterbody_key IN (\n         SELECT waterbody_key FROM whse_basemapping.fwa_lakes_poly WHERE area_ha >= 2)"

# Discharge-based model, as for a `mad` watershed group
frs_habitat_predicates(sp_params, model = "mad")$spawn
#> [1] "((s.edge_type IN (1000, 1100, 2000, 2300) AND s.waterbody_key IS NULL AND s.gradient BETWEEN 0 AND 0.0549 AND s.mad_m3s BETWEEN 0.164 AND 9999) OR (s.waterbody_key IN (SELECT waterbody_key FROM whse_basemapping.fwa_rivers_poly) AND s.gradient BETWEEN 0 AND 0.0549 AND s.mad_m3s BETWEEN 0.164 AND 9999))"

# A small stream passes when a 3 m3/s river is within 1 km downstream
sp_params$params_sp$rules$rear <- list(list(
  edge_types_explicit = c(1000, 1100),
  near_river = list(discharge_min = 3, distance_max = 1000)))
frs_habitat_predicates(sp_params,
  near_river_table = "working.streams_habitat_near_river")$rear
#> [1] "((s.edge_type IN (1000, 1100) AND s.gradient BETWEEN 0 AND 0.0549 AND (s.channel_width BETWEEN 1.5 AND 9999 OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM working.streams_habitat_near_river n WHERE n.id_segment = s.id_segment AND n.watershed_group_code = s.watershed_group_code AND n.measure = 'discharge' AND n.threshold = 3 AND n.distance_max = 1000 AND n.dist_m <= 1000))))"

# The same rule with no mapping inherits the stage's pair from the
# thresholds CSV (here a 20 m channel within 1 km, under cw)
sp_params$params_sp$rules$rear[[1]]$near_river <- NULL
sp_params$params_sp$near_river$rear <- list(measure = "channel_width",
  channel_width_min = 20, distance_max = 1000)
frs_habitat_predicates(sp_params,
  near_river_table = "working.streams_habitat_near_river")$rear
#> [1] "((s.edge_type IN (1000, 1100) AND s.gradient BETWEEN 0 AND 0.0549 AND (s.channel_width BETWEEN 1.5 AND 9999 OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM working.streams_habitat_near_river n WHERE n.id_segment = s.id_segment AND n.watershed_group_code = s.watershed_group_code AND n.measure = 'channel_width' AND n.threshold = 20 AND n.distance_max = 1000 AND n.dist_m <= 1000))))"
